```kn
fn total(lines: list[Line] count <=50) -> money[USDc]
  lines.sum(l => l.price * l.qty)
```

#### `next`

Total: it answers every input in the ranges it declares. Its head writes no effect: this is what kaname infers.

```kn
fn next(order: Order, event: Event) -> result[Order, string]
  match order
    cart c =>
      match event
        add a =>
          if c.lines.count() < 50
            ok(Order.cart { lines: c.lines.append(a.line) })
          else
            err("a cart holds 50 lines")
        remove r => ok(Order.cart { lines: c.lines.filter(l => l.sku != r.sku) })
        place p =>
          if c.lines.count() = 0
            err("an empty cart is not placed")
          else
            ok(Order.placed { lines: c.lines, total: total(lines: c.lines), on: p.on })
        cancel x => ok(Order.cancelled { reason: x.reason })
        else => err("a cart is placed first")
    placed p =>
      match event
        pay y =>
          if y.amount = p.total
            ok(Order.paid { lines: p.lines, on: p.on })
          else
            err("the amount is not the total")
        cancel x => ok(Order.cancelled { reason: x.reason })
        else => err("a placed order is paid or cancelled")
    paid d =>
      match event
        ship s => ok(Order.shipped { lines: d.lines, tracking: s.tracking })
        else => err("a paid order is shipped")
    shipped, cancelled => err("the order is closed")
```

#### `replay`

Total: it answers every input in the ranges it declares. Its head writes no effect: this is what kaname infers.

```kn
fn replay(events: list[Event]) -> result[Order, string]
  let start : result[Order, string] = ok(Order.cart { lines: [] })
  events.reduce(start, (r, e) => after(r: r, event: e))
```

#### `after`

Total: it answers every input in the ranges it declares. Its head writes no effect: this is what kaname infers.

```kn
fn after(r: result[Order, string], event: Event) -> result[Order, string]
  match r
    ok o => next(order: o, event: event)
    err why => err(why)
```

#### `open`

Total: it answers every input in the ranges it declares. Its head writes no effect: this is what kaname infers.

```kn
fn open(order: Order) -> bool
  match order
    shipped, cancelled => false
    else => true
```

## Examples

`kaname check` runs each line of `examples` in the reference interpreter, as a host would call the function, and compares the answer with the one written. The reference interpreter answers these.

```kn
total(lines: [Line { sku: "pen", qty: 2, price: 150USDc }, Line { sku: "ink", qty: 1, price: 400USDc }])
  = 700USDc
next(order: Order.cart { lines: [] }, event: Event.place { on: 2026-10-22 })
  = err("an empty cart is not placed")
next(order: Order.placed { lines: [Line { sku: "pen", qty: 2, price: 150USDc }], total: 300USDc, on: 2026-10-22 }, event: Event.pay { amount: 300USDc })
  = ok(Order.paid { lines: [Line { sku: "pen", qty: 2, price: 150USDc }], on: 2026-10-22 })
replay(events: [Event.add { line: Line { sku: "pen", qty: 2, price: 150USDc } }, Event.place { on: 2026-10-22 }, Event.pay { amount: 250USDc }])
  = err("the amount is not the total")
open(order: Order.cancelled { reason: "late" })
  = false
```
